title: Knots and bursts
caption: The galaxies NGC 4858 and NGC 4860 in the Coma Cluster, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 4858, NGC 4860 · constellation Coma Berenices · about 300 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Two galaxies dominate this Hubble frame. The brighter one, at the center, is NGC 4860, an elliptical galaxy. To its left is NGC 4858, a spiral with a tangled, fiery look. Both belong to the Coma Cluster in the northern constellation Coma Berenices (Berenice's Hair), where more than a thousand galaxies are held together by gravity.

Many of the cluster's members are ellipticals, but its outer parts also hold younger spirals. NGC 4858 is an unusual case. Astronomers call it a galaxy aggregate, a central galaxy ringed by a few bright knots of material that seem to grow out of it, stretching and breaking away and reshaping it as they go.

It is also forming stars at a very high rate, possibly set off by an earlier encounter with another galaxy. At this pace it will run out of gas long before the end of its life. Its knots glow bright red, the color of hydrogen gas energized by the many hot young stars inside them.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.65 x 1.97 arcminutes) and distance (300 million light years), the frame spans roughly 231,000 × 172,000 light-years. Its light set out about 300 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 recorded this pair through very broad filters in visible light. The red knots are glowing hydrogen, but the filter-to-color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: These galaxies are far too faint to see without a large telescope, and Hubble's exposures gather much more light than the eye.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The picture comes from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, an instrument designed to study how stars and galaxies developed in the early Universe. The two galaxies lie about 300 million light-years away.
alt: A bright elliptical galaxy at the center with a smaller, tangled spiral galaxy to its left dotted with bright red knots.
